title: Svante Janson, Tibetan Calendar Mathematics, 2007 revised 2014

source_notes.paraphrase: 67 lunar months equal 65 mean solar months; 24 leap months every 65 years.
source_notes.source_kind: modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript

source_notes.paraphrase: Civil calendar days begin at dawn; tithi spans twelve degrees of lunar-solar elongation.
source_notes.source_kind: modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript

source_notes.paraphrase: Solar-month offset M*=12(Y−Y0)+M−3; fractional true-month argument is (67M*+β*)/65.
source_notes.source_kind: modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript
modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript

source_notes.paraphrase: Phugpa leap months occur at preliminary intercalation index 48 or 49.
source_notes.source_kind: modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript

source_notes.paraphrase: Phugpa regular-month count uses threshold 48; leap month count floors the fraction.
source_notes.source_kind: modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript

source_notes.paraphrase: Tsurphu example epochs 1732/1852 have β*=59/14 respectively.
source_notes.source_kind: modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript

source_notes.paraphrase: Tsurphu leap months have index 0 or 1 and use a distinct integer-count rule.
source_notes.source_kind: modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript

source_notes.paraphrase: Animal month 1 is Dragon in Phugpa but Tiger in Tsurphu.
source_notes.source_kind: modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript

source_notes.paraphrase: Phugpa and Tsurphu compute month elements with different formulas and cycle origins.
source_notes.source_kind: modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript

source_notes.paraphrase: Year power element cycles Wood,Fire,Earth,Iron,Water, each twice, with sexagenary animal.
source_notes.source_kind: modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript

source_notes.paraphrase: Central, life and power mewa numbers derive from (2−Y),(8−Y),(5−Y) amod9.
source_notes.source_kind: modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript

source_notes.paraphrase: Life, body, fortune and spirit elements follow animal/trine and thirty/sixty-year rules.
source_notes.source_kind: modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript

source_notes.paraphrase: Lunar-day animal, trigram and number use separate modular formulas tied to month.
source_notes.source_kind: modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript

source_notes.paraphrase: Calendar-day elements, animals, trigrams and squares use Julian day, not lunar-day indices.
source_notes.source_kind: modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript

source_notes.paraphrase: Tsurphu day mewa changes count direction at solstices; not Phugpa's simple day cycle.
source_notes.source_kind: modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript

source_notes.paraphrase: Mean and computed 'true' longitudes are model positions, not exact modern sky coordinates.
source_notes.source_kind: modern mathematical derivation, not an original Tibetan manuscript

notable_inference: Paper's formulas and existence of independent OSS reference libraries make a bounded deterministic year/month/day calculator preferable to inventing one from scratch.
precision_warning: The paper's computed 'true' longitudes represent a traditional model, not precise physical ephemeris positions.
Do not substitute Gregorian civil year for actual Tibetan calendar year before Losar.
Janson month animal labels differ materially between Phugpa and Tsurphu: month1 Dragon versus Tiger.
Only Tsurphu calendar-day mewa undergoes the solstice reversal described in Remark37.
A correctly reproduced traditional calendar is NOT human personality/outcome predictive validation.
